_comment: Bambu Lab P1S. Connection details are NOT in this file and must not be added: the IP, LAN access code and serial are per-printer and per-person, they live in the encrypted config store as BAMBU_IP / BAMBU_CODE / BAMBU_SERIAL, and a profile is committed to the repository. Issue #73. This profile carries NO machine_start_gcode or machine_end_gcode, deliberately: Daedal Studio does not start prints on Bambu firmware (BambuOperator.start_print refuses), so no start sequence authored here would ever run. Bambu Studio supplies the machine's own. The geometry below is what this file is for — the printability gate reads it.

_sources.machine_geometry: Bambu Lab P1S published specification: 256 x 256 x 256 mm build volume, 0.4 mm stock hotend, enclosed, textured PEI plate. Verified against the printer in the room (owner, 2026-09-09); the machine reports nozzle_diameter '0.4' over MQTT (2026-09-17).
_sources.firmware_verified_against: 01.09.01.00 - the version on the machine. Verified reachable on 2026-09-17: MQTT 8883 authenticates with bblp + access code (CONNACK Success) and implicit FTPS 990 logs in. Bambu tightens third-party LAN access between releases and cannot be downgraded, so this profile is a claim about that firmware.
_sources.temperatures: Conventional PLA values, NOT vendor-derived, and they do not reach this machine. Under the 3MF handoff route Bambu Studio applies its own material profile, so these only affect a G-code file a person may download and inspect. Issue #73's acceptance criterion 5 asked for Bambu Studio-derived values 'copied and cited'; it was withdrawn rather than met, because meeting it means copying AGPL-3.0 content into an Apache-2.0 repository (#73, comment of 2026-09-17).
_sources.material_diameter: 1,75 mm is the P1S's filament format - the machine's PTFE path and extruder are 1,75 mm and so is Bambu's own filament; the 2,85 mm default in fdmprinter.def.json and fdmextruder.def.json describes no machine this project supports. Like the temperatures, it does not reach this machine: under the 3MF handoff route Bambu Studio re-slices and applies its own material profile, so this value only affects a G-code file a person may download and inspect. It is stated anyway because the E axis of that file is wrong without it - sliced on the 2,85 mm default a printer deposits (1,75/2,85)^2, about 38 %, of the intended volume - and because pythonsrc/pipeline.py reads the key to convert extruded length into the filament mass on the telemetry row (#186).
_sources.start_end_gcode: REMOVED, not omitted. Printing a raw gcode_file would run this block instead of the machine's, and the machine's is a firmware-evaluated conditional (M1002 judge_flag / M622 J1 ... M623) on a flag the print command sets - so no start block authored here can invoke the P1S's bed levelling, nozzle wipe or resonance calibration. PR #148 reverted the first attempt over exactly that. BambuOperator.start_print now refuses instead.
_sources.fit_offsets: fit offsets: class 'tuned' in pythonsrc/fit_offsets.py, which is where the citations live. The bands are sourced (docs/dimension-kb-research.md §5 for the 0,2-0,4 mm friction lip, §3 for the 1,5-2 and 4-6 mm cavity clearances) and so are the class accuracies (§6: ±0,1 mm typical tuned and shrink-compensated, ±0,5 % with a ±0,5 mm floor for a general desktop FDM machine); the placement of each number inside its band is this project's reasoning, not a measurement, and fit_offsets.py says so in those words. Nothing here is a compile input - issue #89 decided (b), so these pre-fill the composer and the geometry is not a function of this file.
